chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Fadalah from Aban from Ishaq ibn 'Ammar said:

I said to Abu Ibrahim (peace be upon him): A man has dinars owed to him by another man, so he takes dirhams from him, then the exchange rate changes. He said: 'It is for him at the rate at which he took them from him on that day. And if he took dinars, and there are no dirhams with him, then his dinars are upon him; he takes them by their heads (principal) whenever he wishes.'
ai.seo_question: How should a debt be repaid if the currency exchange rate changes between the time the debt was incurred and the time of repayment?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the rules of debt settlement when currencies differ, establishing that if a creditor accepts dirhams for a dinar debt, the value is fixed at the exchange rate of that specific day, protecting against future fluctuations. Conversely, if the debt remains in dinars, the creditor retains the right to demand the principal amount ('heads') at any time, emphasizing the stability of the original contractual obligation. This ruling highlights the Shia jurisprudential focus on fairness in financial transactions and the prevention of riba (usury) through precise valuation at the time of exchange.
